question:
Classify each of the following as an ordinary differential equation or a partial differential equation. Give reason for your classification:
(i) $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+x\frac{dy}{dx}+y=0$
(ii) $\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0$
(iii) $t\frac{d^2s}{dt^2}+\frac{ds}{dt}=s$.
explanation:
Step 1: Use the basis of classification
A differential equation involving derivatives with respect to only one independent variable is an ordinary differential equation. Equations involving derivatives with respect to more than one independent variable are called partial differential equations.
Step 2: Classify equation (i)
All derivatives of $y$ are with respect to the single independent variable $x$. Hence, it is an ordinary differential equation.
Step 3: Classify equation (ii)
The dependent variable $u$ is differentiated with respect to both $x$ and $y$. Thus, more than one independent variable is involved, so it is a partial differential equation.
Step 4: Classify equation (iii)
All derivatives of $s$ are with respect to the single variable $t$. Hence, it is an ordinary differential equation.
Step 5: Final answer
The classifications are ordinary, partial and ordinary respectively.

options.A:
(i) Ordinary differential equation
(ii) Partial differential equation
(iii) Ordinary differential equation
options.B:
(i) Partial differential equation
(ii) Ordinary differential equation
(iii) Partial differential equation
options.C:
(i) Ordinary differential equation
(ii) Ordinary differential equation
(iii) Partial differential equation
options.D:
(i) Partial differential equation
(ii) Partial differential equation
(iii) Ordinary differential equation
